/-!
# Conjecture 7.23

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given list of group identities,
whether the elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble (that is,
decidable), that is, by A. P. Zamyatin (*Algebra and Logic* **17**, no. 1 (1978), 13–17),
whether this variety is abelian?

A group identity is an equation $u = v$ between two words in the variables
$x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies it if $u$ and $v$ take the same value
for every substitution of elements of $G$ for the variables. The variety given by a
list of identities is the class of all groups satisfying every identity in the list.
Zamyatin proved that the elementary theory of a variety of groups is decidable if and
only if the variety is abelian, so the problem asks whether the set of finite lists of
identities whose variety is abelian is decidable.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- A. P. Zamyatin, *A non-abelian variety of groups has an undecidable elementary theory*,
  Algebra and Logic **17** (1978), 13–17.
-/

blocks.code: abbrev GroupIdentity : Type := List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool)
blocks.docstring:
A group identity $u = v$, given syntactically as a pair of words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$. The word `[(i, true), (j, false)]` stands for
$x_i x_j^{-1}$, as in `FreeGroup.mk`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FreeGroup ℕ × FreeGroup ℕ` (not Primcodable; a quotient, not syntactic input), and Mathlib's `FirstOrder.Language` (no group language or decidability of theories).
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.23».GroupIdentity
justification.why_needed: An algorithm needs a syntactic (Primcodable) representation of a group identity u = v; Mathlib has no notion of a group identity/law. Defined as an abbrev for `List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool)` (pairs of words in the sense of `FreeGroup.mk`), which inherits the standard Primcodable instance.

blocks.name: GroupIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A group identity $u = v$, given syntactically as a pair of words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$. The word `[(i, true), (j, false)]` stands for

abbrev GroupIdentity : Type := List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool)

blocks.code:
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.1) = FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.2)
blocks.docstring:
A group `G` satisfies the identity $u = v$ if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in `G` for
every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Searched Mathlib GroupTheory/Algebra.Group for 'variety', 'law', 'identity', 'verbal'; nothing applicable. `FreeGroup.lift`/`FreeGroup.mk` are used as the building blocks.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.23».SatisfiesIdentity
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a group satisfying a law/identity. Defined as: for every substitution `f : ℕ → G`, `FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk u) = FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk v)`.

blocks.name: SatisfiesIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity $u = v$ if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in `G` for
every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.1) = FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.2)

blocks.code:
def IsAbelianVariety (L : List GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ e ∈ L, SatisfiesIdentity G e) → IsMulCommutative G
blocks.docstring:
The variety of groups given by the list of identities `L` is abelian: every group
satisfying all the identities in `L` is commutative.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No variety-of-groups notion in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib; `IsMulCommutative` is used for 'abelian'.
justification.name: Kourovka.«7.23».IsAbelianVariety
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a variety of groups defined by identities. Defined as: every group `G : Type` satisfying all identities in the list is `IsMulCommutative`. Two API tests (empty list is not abelian; the identity x₀x₁ = x₁x₀ is) are proven.

blocks.name: IsAbelianVariety
blocks.text:
/-- The variety of groups given by the list of identities `L` is abelian: every group

def IsAbelianVariety (L : List GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ e ∈ L, SatisfiesIdentity G e) → IsMulCommutative G

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem not_isAbelianVariety_nil : ¬ IsAbelianVariety [] := by
  intro h
  have := (h (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (by simp)).is_comm.comm (Equiv.swap 0 1) (Equiv.swap 1 2)
  revert this
  decide
blocks.docstring: The empty list of identities gives the variety of all groups, which is not abelian.

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isAbelianVariety_comm :
    IsAbelianVariety [([(0, true), (1, true)], [(1, true), (0, true)])] := by
  intro G _ h
  refine ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
  have := h _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) (fun n => if n = 0 then a else b)
  simpa [FreeGroup.lift_mk] using this
blocks.docstring: The single identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ gives the variety of abelian groups.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question: is the set of finite lists of group identities (words/pairs of words in a free group on countably many generators) whose variety is abelian (i.e. every group satisfying the list is commutative, equivalently [x,y]=1 follows from the list) a decidable (recursive) set — 'soluble' here means algorithmically decidable, not group-theoretically solvable; the 'that is … abelian' clause is not a separate question but the statement's own reformulation via Zamyatin's theorem (a group variety has decidable elementary theory iff it is abelian), so the abelian form is the intended Prop (e.g. `answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred (fun L => variety of L is abelian)`), with the input list implicitly finite.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same faithful core Prop `answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred (fun L => ∀ G : Type [Group G], (∀ identity ∈ L, ∀ f : ℕ → G, lift f (mk u) = lift f (mk v)) → IsMulCommutative G)`; verified FreeGroup.lift_mk semantics, ComputablePred definition, Primcodable instance, answer direction, and boundary cases (empty list = all groups, predicate false; commutation law gives abelian variety). c08 chosen as the cleanest: readable bespoke definitions (GroupIdentity, SatisfiesIdentity, IsAbelianVariety), docstrings citing Zamyatin, two proved `category test` theorems covering both boundary behaviours, AMS 3 20. Only cosmetic edits (variable rename). Compiles with only the `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.

/-!
# Conjecture 7.23

by A. V. Kuznetsov

Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given list of group identities,
whether the elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble (that is,
decidable), that is, by A. P. Zamyatin (*Algebra and Logic* **17**, no. 1 (1978), 13–17),
whether this variety is abelian?

A group identity is an equation $u = v$ between two words in the variables
$x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$; a group $G$ satisfies it if $u$ and $v$ take the same value

list of identities is the class of all groups satisfying every identity in the list.

only if the variety is abelian, so the problem asks whether the set of finite lists of

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- A. P. Zamyatin, *A non-abelian variety of groups has an undecidable elementary theory*,
  Algebra and Logic **17** (1978), 13–17.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.23»

/-- A group identity $u = v$, given syntactically as a pair of words in the letters
$x_i^{\pm 1}$, $i \in \mathbb{N}$. The word `[(i, true), (j, false)]` stands for
$x_i x_j^{-1}$, as in `FreeGroup.mk`. -/
abbrev GroupIdentity : Type := List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool)

/-- A group `G` satisfies the identity $u = v$ if $u$ and $v$ take the same value in `G` for
every substitution `f` of elements of `G` for the variables $x_0, x_1, x_2, \dots$. -/
def SatisfiesIdentity (G : Type*) [Group G] (e : GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ f : ℕ → G, FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.1) = FreeGroup.lift f (FreeGroup.mk e.2)

/-- The variety of groups given by the list of identities `L` is abelian: every group
satisfying all the identities in `L` is commutative. -/
def IsAbelianVariety (L : List GroupIdentity) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], (∀ e ∈ L, SatisfiesIdentity G e) → IsMulCommutative G

/--
Does there exist an algorithm which decides, for a given (finite) list of group identities,
whether the elementary theory of the variety given by this list is soluble (decidable)?
By Zamyatin's theorem (*Algebra and Logic* **17**, no. 1 (1978), 13–17), a variety of
groups has a decidable elementary theory if and only if it is abelian, so the question
is whether there is an algorithm deciding, for a given list of group identities, whether
the variety given by this list is abelian.

Formally: is the predicate "the variety given by `L` is abelian" on finite lists `L` of
group identities a computable predicate?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.23» : answer(sorry) ↔ ComputablePred IsAbelianVariety := by
  sorry

/-- The empty list of identities gives the variety of all groups, which is not abelian. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem not_isAbelianVariety_nil : ¬ IsAbelianVariety [] := by
  intro h
  have := (h (Equiv.Perm (Fin 3)) (by simp)).is_comm.comm (Equiv.swap 0 1) (Equiv.swap 1 2)
  revert this
  decide

/-- The single identity $x_0 x_1 = x_1 x_0$ gives the variety of abelian groups. -/
@[category test, AMS 3 20]
theorem isAbelianVariety_comm :
    IsAbelianVariety [([(0, true), (1, true)], [(1, true), (0, true)])] := by
  intro G _ h
  refine ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩
  have := h _ (List.mem_singleton_self _) (fun n => if n = 0 then a else b)
  simpa [FreeGroup.lift_mk] using this

end Kourovka.«7.23»

items: 'Soluble' elementary theory is read as 'decidable'; per the statement's own 'that is … abelian' clause (Zamyatin 1978) and the decomposition table, the formalized predicate is 'the variety given by the list is abelian', not a direct formalization of decidability of the first-order theory (which would need first-order logic of groups and a Primcodable encoding of sentences, absent from Mathlib).

A group identity is represented as a pair of (unreduced) words `u = v` in `List (ℕ × Bool)` (the input type of `FreeGroup.mk`), i.e. an equation between words in countably many variables x₀, x₁, …. The alternative representation by single words `w = 1` gives a computably equivalent decision problem.

'Algorithm which decides' is formalized as Mathlib's `ComputablePred` with respect to the standard `Primcodable` encoding of `List (List (ℕ × Bool) × List (ℕ × Bool))`; decidability does not depend on the choice of reasonable encoding.

'The variety is abelian' quantifies over groups `G : Type` (universe 0), consistent with the other Kourovka files. This loses nothing: a non-abelian group in the variety has a countable non-abelian subgroup, which is also in the variety and lives in `Type`.
Boundary case: the empty list denotes the variety of all groups, for which the predicate is false (proven as a test), matching the informal reading.

reviewer_notes: Modeling: 'soluble' read as algorithmically decidable; per the statement's own 'that is … abelian' clause (Zamyatin 1978: a group variety has decidable elementary theory iff abelian) the formalized predicate is 'the variety given by the finite list is abelian', not a direct formalization of decidability of the first-order theory (Mathlib has no Primcodable encoding of group sentences). Identities are pairs of raw words in List (ℕ × Bool) (the FreeGroup.mk syntax) over countably many variables; unreduced words are harmless since satisfaction factors through FreeGroup.mk, and any reasonable encoding gives a computably equivalent decision problem (c02's single-word 'w = 1' encoding is equally valid). Quantification over G : Type is harmless (a non-abelian member of the variety has a 2-generated non-abelian subgroup in the variety). No candidate omitted the slot; no objections to the decomposition were raised, and I concur with it.
